text:
jordan.sales: Heads-up: POC with Acme hitting 403 on /v1/generate after a few hours of testing. They say token rotation, but logs show org_mismatch. Can someone triage? cc @luca.eng @sophie.support

sophie.support: On it, grabbing logs. Which key are they using — POC key or org admin key?

jordan.sales: They pasted 'project:key-ABC123' from the onboarding email. Asked for full request dump.

luca.eng: If it's org_mismatch we should check X-Redwood-Org/X-Redwood-Project headers and token->org binding. Also verify scopes quickly.

maya.eng: @jordan can you paste the curl they ran?

jordan.sales: Customer paste: ```curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer ABC123' -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hi"}'``` Response: `403 {"error":"org_mismatch","detail":"token org 999 != request org 123"}`

sophie.support: Confirming in our logs: token bound to org 999, request included header X-Redwood-Org:123 — that's the mismatch. They likely copied an old header from their UI.

luca.eng: Can you run token introspect? Example: ```POST /oauth/introspect
Authorization: Basic <client_creds>
body: token=ABC123``` returns e.g. `{\n  "active": true,\n  "org_id": "999",\n  "projects": ["proj-1"],\n  "scopes": ["inference:generate"]\n}`

maya.eng: Also note sometimes keys rotated and the new key has different scopes. If introspect shows only "inference:read" they'll get 403 on write endpoints.

acme-poc-bot: customer: We rotated keys yesterday for security. Our frontend still sets X-Redwood-Org to the old workspace id. Trying to flip to new key now.

sophie.support: Repro'd locally with their token, same 403. Quick remediation: 1) remove X-Redwood-Org header so token binding is used, or 2) use the token issued for org 123. Sent steps to customer.

raj.sec: Also double-check they didn't use an SSO/partner demo key by mistake — happens in org migrations. Good to confirm token creation audit.

jordan.sales: Customer says their CI rotates keys nightly; UI didn't propagate new org id. So combination of rotation + sticky header.

luca.eng: Filed ticket O-432 to add a clearer error message and telemetry for org/header mismatch to reduce confusion.

maya.eng: Minor note: in introspect we saw the token scopes included only ["inference:read"] in one case — that explains why some calls were 403 even without org mismatch. Asking customer to confirm scopes.

sophie.support: Sent follow-up with three checks: introspect output (redacted), remove custom org header, and verify token scopes. Also gave a one-line curl to test: ```curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer NEWKEY' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health```

deploy-bot: Canary proxies updated to include more explicit "org_mismatch" guidance in error details in next rollout (roll 4/7).

sophie.support: Customer applied new key + removed header and reports 200s again — sending KB with best practices.

jordan.sales: Awesome — I'll update the deal notes and bump SMA for POC since this was operational overhead. Thanks all :tada: :thumbsup:

sophie.support: Follow-ups: attaching ticket IDs and sending final repro to docs team for KB. Owner: sophie.support.
